note: Re-audited independently against RFC 5072 Section 4.1 case 2 ('If an IEEE global identifier is not available, a different source of uniqueness should be used. Suggested sources of uniqueness include link-layer addresses, machine serial numbers, et cetera. In this case, the "u" bit of the interface identifier MUST be set to zero (0).'). TestIPv6CPLocallyAdministeredMACClearsUniversalBit supplies a non-IEEE locally-administered 48-bit link-layer MAC (02:11:22:33:44:55, U/L bit 1) to TentativeIPv6CPInterfaceID (ipv6cp_client.go) and asserts both octet 0 bit 0x02 == 0 and exact modified EUI-64 {0x00, 0x11, 0x22, 0xff, 0xfe, 0x33, 0x44, 0x55} (removing or breaking the XOR with ipv6cpUniversalLocalBitMask fails deterministically). TestIPv6CPTentativeInterfaceIDHasUniversalBitClear proves the non-IEEE fallback/server generator (generateIPv6CPInterfaceID in ipv6cp.go and requestIPv6CPInterfaceID in ncp.go) clears canonical bit 6 (octet 0 mask 0x02) across 256 random draws, retries a scripted {0x02, 0...} draw instead of emitting all-zero, and sends octet 0 = 0x00 on the wire in the initial IPv6CP Configure-Request. TestIPv6CPGlobalEUI48TentativeIdentifierSetsUniversalBit (doc comment edited require. -> mandate., assertions unchanged) provides the contrasting case-1 negative: a globally unique EUI-48 MAC (00:11:22:33:44:55) produces modified EUI-64 {0x02, 0x11, 0x22, 0xff, 0xfe, 0x33, 0x44, 0x55} with u bit 1, failing if bit 0x02 is unconditionally cleared.
